title: Quadratic Response-Surface Analysis of Tensile Strength and Vickers Hardness in Robotic ER5356 Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing
content: This study evaluates the effects of welding current, welding speed, and wire feed speed on the tensile strength (TS) and Vickers hardness (HV0.1) of ER5356 aluminum walls fabricated by robotic wire arc additive manufacturing (WAAM). A face-centered central composite design comprising 19 runs, including five centerpoint runs, was used over ranges of 90–100 A, 3–5 mm/s, and 4–6 m/min. Separate quadratic response-surface models were fitted to the two responses using ordi-nary least squares. The TS model was statistically significant (R² = 0.914, adjusted R² = 0.828; F(9, 9) = 10.64, p = 0.00082), with a nonsignificant lack-of-fit test (p = 0.858). Welding current, wire feed speed, and the quadratic current term were significant at α = 0.05. The HV model was not statis-tically significant (R² = 0.297, adjusted R² = −0.407; F(9, 9) = 0.422, p = 0.893). Run 19 (95 A, 4 mm/s, and 5 m/min) produced the highest measured TS (271.6 MPa), whereas Run 8 (100 A, 5 mm/s, and 6 m/min) produced the highest measured HV (72.5). Cross-sectional imaging showed rounded dark-contrast features, while the examined fracture surfaces displayed dimples and tearing ridges in both selected conditions. The results support a quadratic description of TS within the tested design space, whereas the fitted quadratic model did not establish a significant relationship be-tween the tested factors and HV.
